Step-1:  Moles taken

• CH₃COOH : 0.1 M × 0.500 L = 0.050 mol (weak acid)  
• HCl   : 0.2 M × 0.400 L = 0.080 mol (strong acid → 0.080 mol H⁺)  
• Ba(OH)₂ : 0.3 M × 0.300 L = 0.090 mol Ba(OH)₂  
  Each Ba(OH)₂ gives 2 OH⁻, so n(OH⁻) = 2 × 0.090 = 0.180 mol

Step-2:  Neutralisation of strong acid

OH⁻ first neutralises the strong acid HCl:

0.180 mol OH⁻ – 0.080 mol H⁺ → 0.100 mol OH⁻ remain

Step-3:  Neutralisation of the weak acid

The remaining OH⁻ reacts completely with acetic acid:

CH₃COOH + OH⁻ → CH₃COO⁻ + H₂O  
0.050 mol CH₃COOH + 0.050 mol OH⁻ → 0.050 mol CH₃COO⁻

After this step:

• Excess OH⁻ left = 0.100 – 0.050 = 0.050 mol  
• CH₃COOH is fully consumed; 0.050 mol CH₃COO⁻ produced

Step-4:  Concentration of excess OH⁻

Total final volume = 500 mL + 400 mL + 300 mL = 1200 mL = 1.20 L

[OH⁻] = 0.050 mol / 1.20 L = 0.0417 M

Step-5:  pOH and pH

pOH = –log[OH⁻] = –log(4.17 × 10⁻²) ≈ 1.38  
pH   = 14 – pOH = 14 – 1.38 = 12.62

(The additional OH⁻ generated by acetate hydrolysis is ≈5 × 10⁻⁶ M, negligible compared with 0.042 M.)

Therefore the solution is strongly basic with pH ≈ 12.6.

Answer: C
